summary: The Biomanufacturing Excellence Act of 2025 directs the National Institute of Standards and Technology to award a competitive grant or agreement to establish a National Biopharmaceutical Manufacturing Center of Excellence. The center aims to advance biopharmaceutical manufacturing science, reduce supply chain bottlenecks, support workforce training, and collaborate with educational, industrial, and government partners.

affected_groups.effect: May apply for and receive the competitive grant or agreement to build and operate the Center of Excellence, along with associated funding.
affected_groups.group: Eligible entities (public-private partnerships, higher education institutions, or consortia)

affected_groups.effect: Benefit from workforce training and development programs designed to bolster biotechnology talent.
affected_groups.group: Workers and students in the biotechnology sector

affected_groups.effect: Can engage with the Center of Excellence in collaborative research, infrastructure deployment, and the sharing of best practices.
affected_groups.group: Pharmaceutical manufacturers and related research organizations

key_provisions: Requires the Director of the National Institute of Standards and Technology to solicit applications and award a grant or agreement to establish and operate the National Biopharmaceutical Manufacturing Center of Excellence within 180 days of enactment.
Authorizes the Center of Excellence to receive funding for facility construction, collaborative scaling research, workforce training programs, and relevant research and development.
Sets eligibility requirements so that applicants may be public-private partnerships, institutions of higher education, or consortia of these entities, but explicitly excludes Federal entities.

Outlines specific selection criteria for the award, including past workforce development performance, leverage of other initiatives, geographic proximity to existing infrastructure, estimated time to impact, and co-investment amounts.
Requires the Director to submit progress, initial establishment, and final reports to Congress, and to publish those reports publicly online.
Directs the Center of Excellence to establish intellectual property guidelines in consultation with similar existing institutions prior to commencing operations.
Authorizes an appropriation of $120,000,000 for fiscal year 2026 to carry out the section.
missing_information: The text does not specify exact long-term funding amounts beyond fiscal year 2026.

The center aims to advance biopharmaceutical manufacturing science, reduce supply chain bottlenecks, support workforce training, and collaborate with educational, industrial, and government partners.
summary_detail.significance: The bill directs $120,000,000 in fiscal year 2026 funding toward a single new national center dedicated to biopharmaceutical manufacturing technology, workforce training, and supply chain self-sufficiency.
